content.definition: Error = Mistake in recognition, measurement, presentation, or disclosure in previously issued financial statements (mathematical mistakes, misapplication of GAAP, oversight)

error_vs_change_in_estimate.error: Mistake (should have known better with info available at time) → Retrospective correction
error_vs_change_in_estimate.change_in_estimate: New information, not mistake → Prospective treatment (no restatement)

content.correction_method: Retrospective restatement (restate prior periods as if error never occurred)

correcting_entry.if_prior_year_closed: Adjust beginning retained earnings of earliest period presented
correcting_entry.entry: DR/CR accounts as needed to correct, with offsetting entry to Retained Earnings

counterbalancing.definition: Errors that self-correct over two accounting periods
counterbalancing.note: Even though self-correct, MUST restate if discovered before self-correction completes

non_counterbalancing.correction: Requires adjusting entry regardless of when discovered

inventory_error_example.error: Year 1 ending inventory overstated $10K. Tax rate 30%.
inventory_error_example.impact_year_1: COGS understated $10K → NI overstated $7K (after tax) → RE overstated $7K
inventory_error_example.impact_year_2: Beginning inv overstated → COGS overstated $10K → NI understated $7K → Error self-corrects by end of Year 2
inventory_error_example.if_discovered_year_2: Before Year 2 closes: Adjust Year 1 RE and inventory. After Year 2 closes (preparing Year 3): No entry needed (already self-corrected).
inventory_error_example.entry_if_discovered_year_2_before_close: DR Retained Earnings $7K, DR Deferred Tax Asset $3K, CR Inventory $10K

depreciation_error_example.error: Failed to record depreciation $5K per year for 3 years. Tax rate 30%.
depreciation_error_example.impact: Expenses understated $15K cumulative → NI overstated $10.5K (after tax) → RE overstated $10.5K
depreciation_error_example.correction_entry: DR Retained Earnings $10.5K, DR Deferred Tax Asset $4.5K, CR Accumulated Depreciation $15K
depreciation_error_example.note: Non-counterbalancing (doesn't self-correct). Requires adjustment whenever discovered.

capitalize_vs_expense_error.expensed_should_capitalize: Asset understated, expenses overstated → Adjust asset, accumulated depreciation, RE
capitalize_vs_expense_error.capitalized_should_expense: Asset overstated, expenses understated → Reduce asset, adjust RE

tax_effects.after_tax_adjustment: Error corrections adjust RE for after-tax effect
tax_effects.deferred_taxes: May need to adjust deferred tax assets/liabilities
tax_effects.example: Overstated revenue $10K. Tax 30%. Correct: DR Revenue $10K, CR AR $10K. DR Deferred Tax Asset $3K, DR RE $7K.

disclosure_requirements: Effect on each financial statement line item and per-share amounts for each prior period presented
Cumulative effect on RE at beginning of earliest period presented
content.materiality: Only material errors require restatement. Immaterial errors may be corrected in current period.

sec_considerations.public_companies: May need to file amended reports (8-K) if material error
sec_considerations.restatement: Distinguish between error restatement and revision (error more serious)

cpa_exam_tips: Error = Mistake → Retrospective correction (restate prior periods)
Change in estimate = New info → Prospective (no restatement)
Counterbalancing errors self-correct over 2 years (but still restate if discovered before self-correction)
Non-counterbalancing errors don't self-correct (always require adjustment)
Adjust beginning RE of earliest period presented
Tax effect: Error corrections after-tax to RE

correction_approach: 4. Adjust beginning RE and restate prior periods
cpa_exam_strategies.inventory_error_shortcut: Ending inv overstated → COGS understated → NI overstated → RE overstated (Year 1). Opposite effect Year 2 (self-corrects).
common_mistakes: Treating error as change in estimate (errors require restatement, estimates don't)
Not restating counterbalancing errors (must restate even if self-correcting)
Forgetting tax effect on RE adjustment
Not revaluing deferred tax accounts when correcting errors

key_points: Error = Mistake → Retrospective restatement (restate prior periods)
Change in estimate = New info → Prospective (no restatement)
Adjust beginning RE of earliest period (after-tax)
Restate comparative statements for all prior periods presented
